Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.test
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.test

Class ExpressionLanguageContractTest

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.test.ExpressionLanguageContractTest
public abstract class ExpressionLanguageContractTest extends Object
What the engine promises for rules in any expression language. A language's test extends this class and supplies the expressions each check needs, written in that language: 
class MyLanguageContractTest extends ExpressionLanguageContractTest {
    protected ExpressionLanguage language() { return new MyLanguage(); }
    protected String alwaysTrue() { return "true"; }
    protected String factEquals(String fact, int value) { return fact + " == " + value; }
    // ... one method for each expression the checks need
}

Every check but evaluateAgreesWithDetail runs rules through an engine, so a language passes only if it works with the engine as users will run it. On the module path, a test module of its own, one that requires the kit, must open the package of the extending test to org.junit.platform.commons. Tests that Surefire patches into the language's own named module need no opens clause: Surefire gives JUnit access to them.

The checks compare numbers in the output by value, so a language whose whole numbers are Longs, as CEL's are, or Doubles, as JsonLogic's and JavaScript's are, needs no conversion to pass on that count. What a language reads is a separate promise, and every language here makes it, whatever its own numbers are: a rule written for 1 is also run against a Long, a Short and a BigDecimal fact, and must fire for all three and not for a 2L one. A language that compares whole numbers by type opts out of that one check with comparesWholeNumbersByValue().

See Also:

    • declareVariableThenFail

      protected @Nullable String declareVariableThenFail(String name, int value)
      Returns an action that declares a variable and then fails the run, as y = 2; Integer.parseInt('not a number') does in MVEL. failedActionVariablesStayLocal checks that a later run doesn't read the variable, as a language that clears its variables only when an action succeeds would let it. The action must declare the variable before it fails: one that fails first declares nothing, and the check proves nothing. By default, null.
      Parameters:
      name - The variable's name
      value - The value it holds
      Returns:
      The action, or null if the language's actions have no variables, which skips the check

    • copyThroughVariable

      protected @Nullable String copyThroughVariable(String key, String fact)
      Returns an action that declares a variable holding a fact's value, and then puts the variable's value into the output map under a key. concurrentRuns runs it in many runs at once, each with its own value, so it is likely to catch an action whose variables every run shares, such as a map compiled into the action or a static: such an action puts another run's value, or fails, when another run changes the variable between its declaring the variable and putting it. By default, null.
      Parameters:
      key - The key to put the value under
      fact - The fact's name
      Returns:
      The action, or null if the language's actions have no variables, which leaves the variable out of concurrentRuns rather than skipping it

    • actionVariablesLastTheRun

      protected boolean actionVariablesLastTheRun()
      Whether a variable an action declares lasts until the end of the run, so that a later rule's action in the same run reads it, as in a language that keeps each run's variables with EvaluationContext.runScoped(java.lang.Object, java.util.function.Supplier<? extends T>). By default, false: a variable stays local to the action that declares it. Returning true turns one part of actionVariablesStayLocal around: a later rule in the same run must read the variable, so the check fails when load() refuses that rule, when it fails the run, or when it reads anything but the variable's value. The rest of the check is unchanged: the variable still mustn't change the facts later actions see, and no later run may read it.
      Returns:
      Whether an action's variables last the run

    • actionSyntaxError

      protected String actionSyntaxError()
      Returns an action with a syntax error, one this language's own compiler rejects. By default, whatever syntaxError() returns, which is a broken action in most languages. Override it when that text is a valid action in this one: the language then compiles it without complaint, and the check fails with nothing but JUnit's "expected RuleCompilationException to be thrown", naming neither the expression nor the hook that supplied it.

      The action must not be blank, and the check fails when it is: the engine rejects a blank action itself, naming the rule, before the language is asked to compile anything, so a blank one would pass the check without the language's compiler ever running. Unlike the @Nullable hooks around it, this one can't be skipped by returning null.

      Returns:
      The action, never blank

    • unusableFactName

      protected abstract @Nullable String unusableFactName()
      Returns a fact name that rules in this language can't refer to. It must not be blank or one of the names the language reserves, as ExpressionLanguage.reservedFactNames() returns them ("output" by default), and the check fails when it is: the engine rejects those names itself, before the language is asked, so they would pass the check without the language's checkFactName ever running. Nor may it be "x", the fact the check's rule reads, and the check fails when it is too.
      Returns:
      The name, or null if every name is accepted

    • usableFactNames

      protected Collection<String> usableFactNames()
      Returns fact names that rules in this language can refer to, such as credit_score2. Each is read by a condition and put into the output by an action, and the check fails if the language rejects the name or the rule doesn't fire. By default, none, which skips the check. List the names a language's users will write, so that a checkFactName stricter than the language itself fails here rather than in every run with that fact.
      Returns:

    • missingFactProperty

      protected abstract @Nullable String missingFactProperty(String fact, String property, int value)
      Returns a condition that reads a property the fact doesn't have, which the language must reject when it loads or runs the rule, rather than evaluate to false. It's usually factProperty(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, int) with the same arguments.

      A language whose own semantics read a missing property as null or undefined, as JsonLogic reads a var that isn't there, returns null. Such a language can't tell a misspelled property from an absent one, whether it reads the fact directly or as the map FactProperties.toData makes of it, so the check would fail it for being faithful to its own rules.

      Parameters:

      property - The property the fact doesn't have
      value - The value to compare it with
      Returns:
      The condition, or null if the language reads a missing property as null or undefined, which skips the check

    • bothConditions

      protected @Nullable String bothConditions(String condition, String other)
      Returns a condition that is true when both conditions are, and evaluates condition before other, as condition && other does in MVEL. nestedRunInsideACondition and nestedRunFailsInsideACondition join factProperty("nest", "value", 7), whose getter starts a run nested inside the condition, with factEquals("x", 1), so that the second read is the one that finds any state the nested run left on the thread. A language that evaluates the right side first isn't checked by them: the first passes it, and the second is skipped when the nested run, stopping at the right side, never reads the getter that makes it fail. By default, null.
      Parameters:
      condition - The condition evaluated first
      other - The condition evaluated second
      Returns:
      The condition, or null if the language's conditions can't require both of two conditions, which skips the checks

      Returns a condition that is true when the shared state changeSharedState(java.lang.String, int) changes holds value, and false, without failing, while it doesn't. sharedStateStaysLocal evaluates it in a run before any action changes the state, in the run whose action makes the change, before that action runs, and in a later run.     • endlessAction

      protected @Nullable String endlessAction()
      Returns an action that runs until its run passes its deadline, and stops then, such as while (true) {} in a language that registers an action with EvaluationContext.onCancel(Runnable) which stops its runtime, or that polls EvaluationContext.isCancelled(). endlessActionStopsAtTimeout runs it with a short run timeout, and checks that the run fails with the timeout well within 30 seconds, without its thread interrupted. An action that never stops leaves the thread that runs it going once the check has failed. By default, null.
      Returns:

    • configure

      protected void configure(RulesEngineBuilder<Map<String,Object>> builder)
      Configures each engine the checks build, for a language that needs what the builder carries to compile its expressions: declared facts, imports or options of its own. By default, nothing. It's called once for each engine, after the kit has started an allMatches engine whose output is a HashMap, and added the language.

      The facts the checks' expressions refer to are x, y, applicant and nest, and the names usableFactNames() returns. The checks supply x as a Boolean, a String, null, an Integer, a Long, a Short and a BigDecimal, y as an Integer, applicant as an ExpressionLanguageContractTest.Applicant, an ExpressionLanguageContractTest.ApplicantBean, a ExpressionLanguageContractTest.WritableApplicant and a Map, nest as a ExpressionLanguageContractTest.Nesting, and each of the names usableFactNames() and unusableFactName() return as the Integer 1. So a language that declares them declares x and applicant as Object, and nest as Object or ExpressionLanguageContractTest.Nesting: the engine fails a run whose fact isn't an instance of its declared type with an IllegalArgumentException, before the language evaluates anything, and the check with it. Nor may the language reserve x, y, applicant or nest, as ExpressionLanguage.reservedFactNames() returns them: every check that builds an engine then fails, before it builds one, with the one message that it reserves them.

      It must not change what the checks depend on, or they fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the language:

      • requireDeclaredFacts(): each run supplies only the facts its check reads, so the engine fails it with an IllegalArgumentException before the language evaluates anything.
      • A declaration of the name unusableFactName() returns: load() checks every declared name with the language, or, for a compiler whose factNamesRead() returns a set, every declared name in it, and the language rejects that one. Most checks then fail to load their rules, with a RuleCompilationException, and the checks that expect a load to fail then pass or fail for reasons unrelated to the language.
      • runTimeout(...): a run that outlasts it fails, and its check with it.
      • maxCopies(...) below 2: two checks make two copies of the rules when they load, which build() refuses with more copies than the limit. A higher limit also caps how many sessions concurrentRuns asks for, so maxCopies(2) hides a newSession() that returns a session twice only after its second call.
      • Another language, or a defaultLanguage(...) other than the language's own name: build() throws an IllegalStateException for an engine with two languages and no default, or with a default that isn't one of its languages. defaultLanguage(language().name()) changes nothing.
      • outputWriter(...): the checks read what an action returned from the output map, where OutputWriter.beansAndMaps() puts it.

      The two checks that need copies made when the rules load, copiesAtLoad and sessionsClosed, set copiesAtLoad(2) after this. compilerClosed sets copiesAtLoad(1), so that each compiler has made a session when the rules load before it's closed; the engine warms up each session that isn't Session.none(), which has nothing to warm up. The two that need a run to make its own copy, sessionClosedWhileAnotherRuns and sessionClosedOnAnotherThread, set copiesAtLoad(0), so a copiesAtLoad set here doesn't change them. sessionClosedWhileAnotherRuns also sets maxCopies(1) after this, so that a run nested in another gets an extra copy, and a limit set here doesn't change it either; concurrentRuns sets none, so a limit set here caps the copies, and the sessions, its runs get. The checks that look at what a run leaves for a later one, actionVariablesStayLocal in its parts with a later run, failedActionVariablesStayLocal, sharedStateStaysLocal and conditionDetail, and those that run a rejected rule a second time, conditionAssignmentRejected, conditionWritesRejected, outputNotReplaceable and missingPropertyFailsTheRun, set maxCopies(1) and copiesAtLoad(0) after this, so that each run gets the one copy, and its sessions, that the run before it used: with two copies made when the rules load, a later run would get the other one. Listeners that don't change the output may be added: the engine only logs what a listener throws, unless it's a fatal Error, but beforeExecute and afterExecute are given the output the checks compare. evaluateAgreesWithDetail builds no engine, and compiles with compileContext() instead: a language that overrides both keeps them consistent.

      Parameters:
      builder - The builder of an engine a check is about to build

    • compileContext

      protected CompileContext compileContext()
      Returns the context evaluateAgreesWithDetail compiles its condition with, since that check compiles it with the language's compiler, outside an engine. By default, LanguageTestContexts.compile(), which has no imports, options or declared facts.

      A language that needs configure(io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.RulesEngineBuilder<java.util.Map<java.lang.String, java.lang.Object>>) to compile needs this too, with the same imports, options and declared facts, which the LanguageTestContexts compile methods take. The condition is factEquals("x", 1), evaluated for an x that is an Integer, a Long, a Short and a BigDecimal.

      Returns:
      The context
